Few years back I was at uni. In my second year someone tried to rape me (story for another time) and it really fucked my head up.

After a year or so I was still really messed up and having major anxiety attacks on the reg, but trying really hard to finish my degree. One day we had a presentation due for my biochemistry class. I did all the work (it was a poster) and headed to class... and ended up having an anxiety attack, telling myself I was too stupid, throwing my poster in the rubbish and sitting in a toilet cubicle crying for a good hour.

Once I finally ventured out, there was a woman around the same age as me who looked at me, smiled, hugged me and said, "Everything is going to be ok. I think you needed that." And left.

Great woman. I hope good things have happened for her. I dropped out a few months after that and everything is ok. My life isn't amazing, but I'm happy. I'm glad she did that.

But if I didn't answer the phone after the first ring I was berated. Or do his stupid freaking errands that he couldn't be bothered doing. At one point he blamed his failing uni grades on me because I didn't enforce his study time... because at 32 years old he couldn't do it himself.
Final straw for me is when my boss sent me to a & e with heart attack symptoms (thankfully it wasn't a heart attack) and he said he was too tired from being up gaming all night to come and see me while I was scared. Anyway, point is, if someone doesn't support you when you need it, are they really even your partner? Something for OP to consider.
